deckTitle: The Pharaoh Script — Psychology of Evil

cards.power: Play to reveal the invisible architecture of your own mind.
cards.lore: First there was the Mother Goddess. Then came the Polytheistic vibration matrix. Now? You worship the Literal Brain-Box. You've been downgraded.
cards.gradeReason: Plays the entire deck before a card is drawn. Meta-inversion jackpot.
cards.artworkPrompt: Watercolor. Uncut sheet glowing under all-seeing pyramid eye. Mood: revelation.

cards.lore: School is hard because it teaches you to ignore your intuition and trust the data. FrizzleBob is hard because he teaches you the data is a psy-op.
cards.gradeReason: Persona clear, but 'epistemic sabotage' needs a warm-up lap to fully land.
cards.artworkPrompt: Pen-and-ink. Frantic rabbit professor at chalkboard labeled PSY-OP. Mood: manic authority.

cards.power: Discard your current worldview. Draw a new, terrifying one.
cards.lore: A class of ideas and concepts. We will build on them throughout the semester. Viewer discretion is heavily, heavily advised.
cards.gradeReason: Discard worldview, draw terror. Tutorial and threat in seven words. Done.
cards.artworkPrompt: Watercolor. Terrified rabbit mid-worldview-swap, old cards dissolving into new ones. Mood: vertigo.

cards.power: Target player realizes they are the punchline.
cards.lore: They turn you into a programmable robot to use as a weapon. Welcome to the uncut sheet.
cards.gradeReason: Target realizes they're the punchline. Table goes quiet. Perfect.
cards.artworkPrompt: Cartoon. Boardroom full of robots all wearing the same face. Mood: punchline delivered.

cards.lore: Before, we understood that mind led to matter. The universe was one giant vibrating mind. Intuition was king.
cards.gradeReason: Interesting reversal, but the power reads like a chess move, not a performance cue.
cards.artworkPrompt: Watercolor. Cosmic owl conducting vibrating atoms of mind-matter. Mood: ancient wisdom.

cards.lore: Today in science class: if you don't see it, it doesn't exist. The brain creates the mind. A highly problematic downgrade.
cards.gradeReason: Losing all intuition points lands once you know what intuition costs.
cards.artworkPrompt: Pen-and-ink. Sheep in lab coat staring at brain jar labeled INTUITION. Mood: clinical dread.

cards.lore: Kant says we can never know true reality (Noumena), only what we see (Phenomena). If they control your experience, they control your memories.
cards.gradeReason: Kant drops in uninvited. Philosophy majors love it. Everyone else needs a handshake.
cards.artworkPrompt: Watercolor. Blindfolded badger in shadows, only Phenomena lit, Noumena lurking behind. Mood: Kantian fog.

cards.lore: How to ensure your legacy? Put the kids on an island, tell them a story, and pump them full of psychedelics. They'll swear it actually happened.
cards.gradeReason: Fake legacy memory via island vacation and mushrooms. You've already done this to your kids.
cards.artworkPrompt: Psychedelic watercolor. Monkey shaman handing mushrooms to confused children on jungle island. Mood: implanted wonder.

cards.power: Attention-Sink. Target skips their next 3 turns studying.
cards.lore: China's solution: the civil service exam. Focus everyone's energy on bureaucracy for social stability. Guess what? It's still around today. We call it the Gaokao.
cards.gradeReason: Three turns studying. Gaokao call-out. Nobody at the table is smiling.
cards.artworkPrompt: Watercolor. Panda army at exam desks under imperial tower, papers flying. Mood: bureaucratic infinity.

cards.power: Pacify entire board. No attacks allowed this turn.
cards.lore: The Indus Valley Civilization created an egalitarian, peaceful prototype for Buddhism. The rare, prosperous pacification protocol.
cards.gradeReason: Good mechanic, but 'egalitarian illusion' is analysis, not invitation.
cards.artworkPrompt: Watercolor. Serene elephant meditating in rainbow Indus Valley, pacification protocol glowing. Mood: rare peace.

cards.power: Perpetual Warfare. All players take 1 damage every turn.
cards.lore: Iraq has no natural defenses. The social glue? Centuries of endless, unifying warfare.
cards.gradeReason: Perpetual warfare as social glue. Everyone takes damage. No one asks why.
cards.artworkPrompt: Cartoon. Animals charging in tornado loop around ziggurat, perpetual damage counter visible. Mood: futile war.

cards.power: Use Target as a God-King Meat-Shield.
cards.lore: Egypt's solution: The Pharaoh is God. The problem? He's human, and his life is constantly at risk. He risk. He needed... adjustments.
cards.gradeReason: God-King Meat-Shield. Needed adjustments. The lore earns every word.
cards.artworkPrompt: Dark watercolor. Cat Pharaoh on throne with skeletal puppet strings from crocodile priests above. Mood: exposed divinity.

cards.lore: Empathy? Respect? Wrong. Great leaders need unpredictability. They are a literal hundred different people depending on the circumstance.
cards.gradeReason: A hundred different people. Alignment switches mid-sentence. You ARE doing this.
cards.artworkPrompt: Watercolor. Chameleon cycling through 100 faces simultaneously at negotiating table. Mood: weaponized chaos.

cards.power: Ignore all incoming damage and public hatred.
cards.lore: The most hated men in the world go to bed and sleep like babies. They wake up happy. They just do not care.
cards.gradeReason: Most hated men alive. Sleep like babies. Don't care. Let's go.
cards.artworkPrompt: Cartoon. Eagle boss sleeping peacefully while angry mob burns torches outside window. Mood: psychopathic serenity.

cards.lore: Lack of empathy. Total selfishness. To survive the game, you must be a psychopath.
cards.gradeReason: Clear concept, but 'void' is more diagnosis than dare.
cards.artworkPrompt: Pen-and-ink. Hyena skeleton labeled ME consuming allies at empty table. Mood: hollow victory.

cards.power: Win the game by cheating the rules.
cards.lore: In a game of millions, you win by cheating via secret alliances. The problem? Everyone knows this. The solution? Multiple personalities so you never betray yourself.
cards.gradeReason: Win by cheating. Multiple personalities so you never betray yourself. Hall of Fame.
cards.artworkPrompt: Dark watercolor. Snake ouroboros of alliance-cheating politicians, crowns passing invisibly. Mood: infinite betrayal.

cards.lore: Ra must kill the serpent Opus every night to prevent a solar eclipse. The Pharaoh is drugged and forced to stab or burn an effigy to program the "Hero" alter.
cards.gradeReason: Gain strength, attack blindly, required to kill a snake nightly. This is your hero.
cards.artworkPrompt: Watercolor. Cat Pharaoh drugged, stabbing serpent effigy while priests nod approvingly. Mood: programmed heroism.

cards.power: Survive lethal damage, but lose a turn.
cards.lore: Tricked into a tomb by Set, then cut into a million pieces. The Pharaoh is locked in a box, humiliated, and traumatized to program the "Passive Victim" alter.
cards.gradeReason: Survive lethal damage. Lose a turn. Tragic box-dweller archetype activated instantly.
cards.artworkPrompt: Dark watercolor. Cat Pharaoh locked in ornate spiked box by smiling Anubis figure. Mood: manufactured victimhood.

cards.power: Retaliate for double damage after taking a hit.
cards.lore: Horus fights Set for the throne via drowning challenges and domination. The Pharaoh is waterboarded to program the "Vengeful Child" alter.
cards.gradeReason: Double damage after being hit. Waterboarded for daddy issues. Retaliation encoded.
cards.artworkPrompt: Action watercolor. Horus cat fighting Set hippo underwater, revenge programming activating. Mood: engineered fury.

cards.lore: The manufactured enemy. He builds the tomb, cuts up the brother, and initiates the drowning. The necessary trauma-inducer for the grand play.
cards.gradeReason: Trigger trauma scripts. The manufactured enemy doing exactly what enemies do.
cards.artworkPrompt: Sinister cartoon. Anubis-Set reading from director's chair labeled THE GRAND PLAY. Mood: scripted evil.

cards.lore: The trusted voice in the dark. A priest wearing the Isis mask comforts the Pharaoh during trauma, becoming the sole controller who whispers commands in the night.
cards.gradeReason: Whispers commands in the dark. Controls your next move. Sweetest nightmare at the table.
cards.artworkPrompt: Watercolor. Ibis-masked handler whispering into sleeping Pharaoh cat's ear in darkness. Mood: intimate control.

cards.lore: Smell is the switch. Incense activates Ra. Roses activate Osiris. The priests flood the throne room with scents to determine how the Pharaoh makes decisions.
cards.gradeReason: Brilliant — scent activates personality — but requires scene-setting before the laugh fully lands.
cards.artworkPrompt: Watercolor. Steampunk scent-machine pumping rose and incense clouds at hypnotized cat king. Mood: olfactory manipulation.

cards.power: Execute a perfect attack while your mind is blank.
cards.lore: If the best soccer player gets amnesia, they still kick the ball perfectly. Subconscious muscle memory. Through programming, anyone can be turned into a killer robot.
cards.gradeReason: Killer robot via soccer amnesia is brilliant but the path needs one more breadcrumb.
cards.artworkPrompt: Cartoon. Amnesiac leopard kicking skull-ball perfectly, mind completely blank. Mood: programmed precision.

cards.power: Sacrifice a leader to start a civil war.
cards.lore: Who runs this? The Priest class. The Deep State. And when factions divide, they simply program the Pharaoh's brother to ignite a civil war. Everyone is programmed.
cards.gradeReason: Sacrifice a leader. Start a civil war. Everyone's programmed. Cue the crocodile robes.
cards.artworkPrompt: Dark watercolor. Crocodile deep state around blood-stained strategic map, Pharaoh-brother pawn in center. Mood: shadow government.

cards.lore: Why would the royals agree to this? NDEs. For 10 minutes, you are literally dead. The priests experiment on themselves via drowning and starvation to hack the spirit realm.
cards.gradeReason: Hurting yourself for cards is dramatic. The NDE-as-spirit-hack angle stays in lore territory.
cards.artworkPrompt: Watercolor. Royal alligator drowned in bathtub, spirit ascending, priests watching with clipboards. Mood: experimental death.

cards.power: Target feels all damage they dealt this game.
cards.lore: There is no difference between Heaven and Hell. It's just the Life Review. Dissociation ends here. You must physically feel the pain you caused others.
cards.gradeReason: Feel every damage you dealt. No Heaven or Hell, just receipts. Instant karma card.
cards.artworkPrompt: Cartoon. Wolf chained to cinema seat watching himself harm others on screen. Mood: karmic horror.

cards.lore: When you do evil, you create negative weight. When you do good, you create upward physical force. You finally see the energy you generated.
cards.gradeReason: Good vs evil as literal physics is beautiful. Power phrasing floats a beat too high.
cards.artworkPrompt: Luminous watercolor. Angel badger floating up in golden light, negative weights falling below. Mood: earned ascension.

cards.power: The only resource that persists after Game Over.
cards.lore: When you die, love is actually a physical force. The more you have, the higher you ascend. Stuck? You have to come back and do it again.
cards.gradeReason: Love as physical force after Game Over. Only card in the deck that hurts.
cards.artworkPrompt: Space watercolor. Wolf spirit ascending cosmos tethered to glowing red heart. Mood: transcendent love.

cards.lore: MK-Ultra: 1950s program led by chemist Sydney Gottlieb. Testing drugs and brainwashing on innocent citizens. They admitted they did it. Just "not anymore".
cards.gradeReason: Brainwash civilian. They admitted it. Just not anymore. Shortest verdict in history.
cards.artworkPrompt: Dark cartoon. Rat scientist with LSD syringe, ancient ankh shadow looming on wall. Mood: state-sanctioned evil.

cards.lore: To test the drugs, the CIA literally set up a brothel. Lure them with sex, dose them with LSD, figure out how to control the mind. Sound familiar?
cards.gradeReason: LSD plus motel plus mind control. The Fixer's favorite operational nightclub.
cards.artworkPrompt: Noir watercolor. Badger spy in motel pouring glowing green liquid into martini glass. Mood: honeytrap protocol.

cards.lore: Psychologists have a greater propensity for mental illness than most people. Your doctor is literally more screwed up than you are. Positive psychology is brainwashing.
cards.gradeReason: Healer poisons you. Your doctor is worse off. Positive psychology is brainwashing. Certified.
cards.artworkPrompt: Cartoon. Pig psychologist prescribing poison from diploma-covered office to confused rabbit patient. Mood: inverted healing.

cards.lore: The theory that you can break a mind so completely it gives up. The military thought they could use it to turn a "Ra" terrorist into an "Osiris" citizen.
cards.gradeReason: Classic concept lands clean. Power is clear but the Ra-to-Osiris flip needs setup.
cards.artworkPrompt: Dark watercolor. Dog curled in cage, all attack options grayed out, HUMBUG burning nearby. Mood: installed defeat.

cards.lore: The military claimed it was "rogue soldiers". The court testimony revealed it was an $80 million CIA psychological design. Enhanced Interrogation.
cards.gradeReason: False confession. $80M psychological design. 'Rogue soldiers' defense never had a chance.
cards.artworkPrompt: Pen-and-ink. Military dogs guarding ancient hieroglyph-covered dungeon. Mood: five-thousand-year deja vu.

cards.lore: Abu Zubaydah's testimony: force-fed, put in a coffin, drowned, threatened with a power drill. It is the EXACT story of Egypt. They are running the 5,000-year-old script.
cards.gradeReason: Re-applying the Osiris Trauma is potent but requires the Egypt arc to be active.
cards.artworkPrompt: Dark watercolor. Bear in orange prison jumpsuit in coffin mirroring ancient Egyptian ceremony. Mood: eternal script.

cards.power: Create an unstoppable enemy on the board.
cards.lore: Human rights groups found that US prisons fueled extremism. ISIS (named after the Egyptian goddess handler) was an American creation, designed to create maximum chaos.
cards.gradeReason: Named after the goddess handler. Made in USA. Unstoppable enemy. Popcorn's ready.
cards.artworkPrompt: Cartoon. Made-in-USA crate exploding open, monster holding ankh cross. Mood: manufactured enemy reveal.

cards.power: Transform a citizen into a weapon.
cards.lore: They thought they were turning Ra into Osiris. They ended up turning Osiris into Ra. How stupid were they? Or... did the experiment work exactly as intended?
cards.gradeReason: Transform citizen into weapon. Or did it work exactly as intended? That question lands.
cards.artworkPrompt: Steampunk watercolor. Citizen-to-weapon factory with Ra and Osiris symbols on inputs and outputs. Mood: intended outcome.

cards.lore: Who built the internet? The US Military. Do you think the DoD built the world's nervous system for free? It's an extraction grid.
cards.gradeReason: Extraction grid premise is solid but the card name doesn't invite performance the way it should.
cards.artworkPrompt: Pen-and-ink. Pentagon wired to glowing globe of fiber optic nerves. Mood: extraction infrastructure.

cards.power: Distract target while stealing their data.
cards.lore: Twitter and Facebook are just the public face. Private billionaires fronting for military data extraction infrastructure.
cards.gradeReason: Distract while stealing data. Billionaire frontmen for military infrastructure. Screenshot this.
cards.artworkPrompt: Cartoon. Lizard in suit dangling thumbs-up hook at mesmerized social media crowd. Mood: data harvest.

cards.lore: What they did in Egypt to one guy, they now do to everyone. Mass education and mass media are the new olfactory triggers. The results of MK-Ultra spread through society.
cards.gradeReason: MK-Ultra for everyone. Olfactory triggers via television. Nobody opted out.
cards.artworkPrompt: Watercolor. Mass of phone-zombified animals in hypnotic TV spirals, incense filling the air. Mood: olfactory mass control.

cards.power: Game Over. You are the product.
cards.lore: Good news guys! Each and every one of you are now the Pharaoh. The exact same mechanisms of trauma and dissociation are right there in your pocket.
cards.gradeReason: Game Over. You are the product. Silence at the table guaranteed.
cards.artworkPrompt: Dark watercolor. Lion looking at phone seeing Pharaoh's reflection, pyramid visible behind. Mood: final revelation.

cards.gradeReason: Powers without lore. This is a caption, not a card. Needs its scene.
cards.artworkPrompt: Pen-and-ink. Egyptian sarcophagus with sensor tubes attached. Mood: ancient technology.

cards.gradeReason: Same structural issue — visual comparison page, not standalone card.
cards.artworkPrompt: Pen-and-ink. CIA sensory deprivation pod mirroring sarcophagus design. Mood: modern archaeology.

cards.gradeReason: Placeholder card. Deep State Alpha needs a lore voice to land.
cards.artworkPrompt: Dark watercolor. Crocodile priests in ritual robes orchestrating kingdom from shadows. Mood: eternal deep state.

cards.gradeReason: Beta mirror of Priest Class. Visual juxtaposition requires the full page to work.
cards.artworkPrompt: Pen-and-ink. Military-industrial boardroom with same crocodile energy, everyone in lab coats. Mood: institutional deja vu.

cards.gradeReason: Atmospheric as part of the curve. Incomplete as standalone.
cards.artworkPrompt: Watercolor. Clean golden retriever standing in light, sequence initiated, no handlers yet. Mood: innocent beginning.

cards.gradeReason: Functional. Better with the step sequence visible.
cards.artworkPrompt: Psychedelic watercolor. Dog exploding into color fragments under electric overload. Mood: identity shatter.

cards.power: The Spirit leaves the physical form.
cards.gradeReason: Evocative visual. Power line alone doesn't activate it.
cards.artworkPrompt: Ethereal watercolor. Ghost dog floating from collapsed body, roses blooming around. Mood: spirit evacuation.

cards.gradeReason: Sequence pays off here. Chilling closer.
cards.artworkPrompt: Dark watercolor. Dog in robotic helmet, rose scents locking new identity in place. Mood: programmed completion.

cards.power: Evade all fact-checkers for one turn.
cards.lore: This is all speculation. It's really important for you to doubt and question me. I have no evidence that this is true. Take it with a grain of salt.
cards.gradeReason: Self-referential disclaimer as weapon. FrizzleBob's finest structural moment.
cards.artworkPrompt: Cartoon. Rabbit holding JUST A THEORY shield deflecting LOGIC arrows. Mood: defensive speculation.

cards.power: Destroy evidence. Remove cards from the discard pile.
cards.lore: Why don't we have proof? Because the most sensitive documentation is always destroyed by the participants. It's the greatest state secret of Egypt, and of the CIA.
cards.gradeReason: Greatest state secret of Egypt and the CIA. Same sentence. Done.
cards.artworkPrompt: Cartoon. Goat in suit shredding hieroglyphic documents next to state seal. Mood: evidence erasure.

cards.power: Assassinate a player with high Empathy.
cards.lore: If you're a nice person who feels sorry for poor people, you're dead. The Pharaoh's brothers want the throne. The priests are actually "protecting" the Pharaoh by making him a psychopath.
cards.gradeReason: Assassinate Empathy. Protecting the Pharaoh by making him a psychopath. Brutal logic.
cards.artworkPrompt: Dark cartoon. Sweet white rabbit surrounded by crosshair laser sights from all angles. Mood: nice-guy trap.

cards.power: Break the fourth wall. Game ends in a draw.
cards.lore: Wait... if the brain creates the mind... and the prompt engineer creates the rabbit... am I just a programmed alter? KAYFABIZARRO!
cards.gradeReason: Fourth wall explodes. Am I a programmed alter? KAYFABIZARRO! Perfect game-ender.
cards.artworkPrompt: Meta watercolor. FrizzleBob rabbit seeing own code on screen, fourth wall shattering. Mood: programmed epiphany.

cards.lore: Train them to shoot while on psychedelics. Say the word "Acadabra". Later, if they hear "Acadabra", they pull the gun. Magic is just programming.
cards.gradeReason: Acadabra activates the sleeper. Magic is just programming. Whole room pauses.
cards.artworkPrompt: Cartoon. Radio bird transforming into armed soldier on trigger word command. Mood: sleeper activation.

cards.power: Overwhelm opponent with a synthetic threat.
cards.lore: The synthetic legacy memory. Transport 100 people to Monkey Island to survive flesh-eating monkeys. They return strong, wise, and united.
cards.gradeReason: Synthetic threat, island survival, legacy memory installed. Chaos theory dressed as field trip.
cards.artworkPrompt: Cartoon. Mob of red-eyed monkeys overwhelming opponents on jungle island. Mood: synthetic threat chaos.

cards.power: Trick an opponent into skipping a turn.
cards.lore: "Look, I built a tomb and it's really comfortable! Let me try!" Osiris jumps in. Set closes the lid. The dumbest god in history.
cards.gradeReason: Osiris is the dumbest god in history. Set smiles. Lid closes. Table erupts.
cards.artworkPrompt: Cartoon. Spiked tomb labeled COZY as Osiris bird happily climbs in with Set smiling. Mood: fatal deception.

cards.lore: Horus and Set turn into hippos and go to the bottom of the river to see who can hold their breath the longest. A completely normal way to choose an Emperor.
cards.gradeReason: Drown opponent. Hippo Emperor selection. A completely normal succession procedure.
cards.artworkPrompt: Cartoon. Cat Pharaoh hippo and Set hippo underwater breath-holding contest. Mood: absurd succession.

cards.power: Blackout the board. No visual attacks.
cards.lore: If Ra forgets to stab Opus the serpent one night? Boom. Solar eclipse. The sun cannot rise. The trauma ritual must be maintained daily.
cards.gradeReason: Daily trauma ritual maintains the sun. Eclipse mechanic is vivid but needs the Ra frame.
cards.artworkPrompt: Watercolor. Egyptian crowd panicking at black sun, sleeping Ra cat visible underground. Mood: maintenance blackout.

cards.power: Retain skill level even when silenced.
cards.lore: If the greatest soccer player gets amnesia and forgets who he is, kick a ball at him and he'll kick it perfectly back. The subconscious is a loyal machine.
cards.gradeReason: Subconscious loyalty is a great concept. Power is functional. Visualization does the heavy lifting.
cards.artworkPrompt: Watercolor. Goat soccer player kicking ball perfectly with completely blank thought bubble. Mood: subconscious loyalty.

cards.lore: Two psychologists paid $80 million to reverse-engineer Egyptian trauma rituals and call it "Learned Helplessness". The most lucrative evil in history.
cards.gradeReason: Most lucrative evil in history. Lore carries, power line underwhelms.
cards.artworkPrompt: Cartoon. Rat holding $80M CIA check outside psychological research cage. Mood: lucrative evil.

cards.power: Restart the game with the exact same rules.
cards.lore: Who we are as humans has not changed in thousands of years. We have not improved on the Egyptians. All modern technology is just doing what they did.
cards.gradeReason: Restart with exact same rules. No improvement on the Egyptians. Final verdict on civilization.
cards.artworkPrompt: Split-panel watercolor. Ancient Egyptian lizard and modern lizard in hoodie: identical posture. Mood: 5000-year glitch.

verdict: The Pharaoh Script is a masterclass in escalation — ancient Egypt's trauma-based kingmaking traced through CIA black sites to your own phone screen. The Egyptian character quartet (Ra/Osiris/Horus/Set) is the strongest role-playing anchor any KK deck has produced, and 'You Are The Pharaoh' is a legitimate table-ender that will silence any room. Only structural weakness: the Cycle of Abuse synthesis page (4 cards without lore) sacrifices playable depth for visual argument — those placeholders frustrate solo play. Table-ready: YES.
blurb: For anyone who wondered why history keeps repeating itself. From Egyptian temples to CIA motel rooms to your TikTok feed — The Pharaoh Script traces five thousand years of psychological programming and leaves you the punchline.

coverQA.coverVisual: 5 — FrizzleBob at the red-string board flanked by burning pyramid and all-seeing eye — chaotic genius that earns every detail
coverQA.coverTitle: 5 — 'THE MASTER COVER / Cut along the dotted lines to sever your attachment to reality!' — perfect threat disguised as craft instruction
coverQA.coverVibeMatch: 5 — delivers exactly what the title promises: institutional paranoia as a Komik Kard
coverQA.coverOriginality: 4 — familiar FrizzleBob conspiracy-board format, but 'sever your attachment to reality' is genuinely new territory
coverQA.coverViral: 5 — the image plus that instruction is an instant screenshot, the four corner-cards add replay value
coverQA.coverNote: This might be the strongest cover in the Secret History run — the 'sever your attachment to reality' instruction doubles as both craft direction and psychological command. The four embedded card panels on the uncut sheet format earn their real estate. FrizzleBob at the red-string board looking genuinely unhinged is the face of this franchise.

notes: 15 pages, 60 cards total including 4 cover-sheet corner cards. Page 11 (Synthesis: Cycle of Abuse) is structured as a comparative visual — 4 cards have POWER text only, no LORE; graded G3 due to incomplete card structure, not weak concept. Page 12 (Dissociation Curve) presents 4 sequential step cards without lore — these function as a narrative sequence and are intentional structural choices. The Ra/Osiris/Horus/Set quartet on page 5 is the conceptual anchor of the entire deck. 'You Are The Pharaoh' (card 40) functions as a deck-closer that reframes every prior card retroactively. No RAF dice boxes visible. No decorative font artifacts detected. The Egyptian script to modern CIA to social media escalation arc is unusually tight for a KK deck of this size.

urgent: Add lore text to 4 synthesis cards: Egyptian Tomb, CIA Black Site, The Priest Class, The Military-Industrial Complex
Add lore text to 4 Dissociation Curve step cards (Step 1-4)
quickWins: 'Military Internet Cables' name is dry — consider renaming to something more performative e.g. 'The Pentagon's Nervous System'
'The $80 Million Invoice' power line ('Steal resources from the bank') undersells the lore — could be 'Bill the taxpayer for your brainwashing program'
niceToHave: Bundle-connect Guantanamo Scripting explicitly with Ra/Osiris setup in gameplay notes to reduce context dependency
'Sever your attachment to reality' from the cover deserves its own standalone card in a future booster

marketingText:
Kayfabizarro: THE PHARAOH SCRIPT – Five Thousand Years of the Psychology of Evil, Dealt Face-Up (Free Cut & Play Comic Card Game)

Memphis, Langley, your feed. Same script, three different costumes.

Power never had to be reinvented. It got inherited, temple to agency to algorithm, the same four-part program running under new management every century. A priest-king carving his face into a wall, a handler renting a motel room, a platform metering your dopamine by the scroll: the costumes change, the grammar of domination does not. The Pharaoh Script lays out the whole inheritance, all five thousand years of it, and saves the punchline for the last card.

This is wrestling for the oldest con there is. You pick up a Pharaoh, you run his move out loud, and the table decides whether the spell holds or snaps the second someone names it. Sixty cut-and-play cards turn five millennia of psychological programming into a match you can actually play, instead of a documentary you nod along to.

WHAT'S INSIDE?
- The Pharaoh Script Core Deck: 60 High-Res "Print, Cut & Play" Cards, featuring The Nice Guy Fatality, Uncle FrizzleBob's Epiphany, and the closer You Are The Pharaoh, the card that retroactively rewrites every move you just performed.
- The Freestyle Rules: The complete Anti-Rulebook. No complicated math, just storytelling, dice-driven chaos, and a straight face held long enough to sell the spell.
- The Secret-History Engine: run the Ra, Osiris, Horus and Set quartet forward through the Cycle of Abuse and down the Dissociation Curve, from Egyptian temple to CIA motel room to the screen in your hand.

THE "LIVING DECK" PASS (Free Updates)
By grabbing this deck, you aren't just buying a static PDF. You are entering the Secret History cycle. Every future volume and topic-specific expansion in this series lands in your library as a FREE update.

WHY "PAY WHAT YOU WANT"?
I draw these because a script you can name is a script you can finally stop running. Are you broke? Enter "0" and take it. Cut it, play it, hand it to the friend who keeps mistaking the choreography for chaos. Want to support the craft? Every dollar goes straight into the ink and the next volume. Share it freely, attribute honestly, never resell it. CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.

Choose your reality. Become an Epistemic Outlaw.
"The script never changed. They just kept reprinting the costumes."
Stay fluffy. — Uncle FrizzleBob
